data.title: Fast stable sulfide electrolytes
constraints: Li diffusion at least as fast as parent

data.goal: Find new sulfide solid electrolytes for lithium-metal batteries, derived from Li7P3S11 or beta-Li3PS4, that conduct lithium at least as fast as their parent and stay stable against lithium metal. Learn from the candidates that fail.

proposals.rationale: Double Cl doping doubles Li vacancies for faster diffusion and forms LiCl interphase stable against Li metal.
Dilute O in Li7P3S11 should form passivating phosphate while preserving sulfide conduction better than higher O content.
Single Na pillar expands Li7P3S11 channels for Li motion with less blocking risk than double Na doping.

reply.hypothesis: Combine Li-vacancy creation by halogens with dilute O passivation and Na expansion to boost conduction and Li-metal stability.

data.text: Iteration 1 tested halogen-driven Li vacancies with dilute O passivation and Na expansion. Li5P2S7Cl, Li14P6S21O and NaLi13(P3S11)2 all passed the stability and insulation filters with energy above the hull of about 0.05, 0.02 and 0.01 eV per atom and band gaps of about 2.6, 2.5 and 2.4 eV. All three failed slow tests: Li5P2S7Cl showed framework motion with Cl diffusing at 17.7 percent of Li, Li14P6S21O showed framework motion with O diffusing at 5.3 percent of Li, and NaLi13(P3S11)2 was non-passivating against Li metal with a reaction of 2.44 eV per atom forming metallic Na. The agent concluded to limit halogens to one per cell and prefer larger Br or I, avoid isolated O in favor of clustered PO4-like units or isovalent Se, and drop Na mixing for non-reducible Mg vacancy or P-site As Sb substitutions, prioritizing dilute isovalent Se and As plus Mg-vacancy variants on mp-985583 Li3PS4.

data.text: In iteration 3 the agent tested isovalent Se/As expansions on Li3PS4 and a single large Br substitution intended to keep the framework intact on Li13P6S21Br, correcting earlier Cl/O motion issues. Li3PSeS3, Li12As3PS16 and Li13P6S21Br all passed stability and band gap filtering with energy above the hull around -0.01 eV per atom for the first two and 0.03 eV per atom for Li13P6S21Br, and gaps near 2.4 eV, 2.3 eV and 2.4 eV respectively. Molecular dynamics at 600 K showed Li13P6S21Br tied with its parent with diffusion ratio 1.01 Â± 0.20, confirming the intact-framework Br substitution fixes motion, and the agent concluded isovalent As/Se substitutions are the most stable on Li3PS4 and will submit the Se/As candidates to diffusion and Li-contact tests.

reply.executive_summary: The best compromise is Li6P2SeS7 derived from Li3PS4 by replacing S with Se. Its energy above the hull is -0.007 eV/atom with an error bar of 0.005 eV/atom from comparison on 25 known compounds. Its band gap is 2.485 eV and 3.102 eV by a second method. Its electrochemical window is stable from 1.8 V to 2.24 V and it is passivating against lithium metal. Its diffusion coefficient at 600 K is 3.9e-06 cmÂ²/s with an error of 9.6e-07 cmÂ²/s, with a ratio to the parent of 0.657 with an error of 0.211 and a verdict of tied. Its ionic conductivity at 300 K is an extrapolated estimate of order 0.1 mS/cm, value 0.144 mS/cm with a range of 0.025 mS/cm to 0.849 mS/cm, from diffusion at 600 K assuming the parent activation energy of 0.414 eV. Its reaction with LiFePO4 is -0.145 eV/atom. The close Se-substituted family was already studied and no exact report of Li6P2SeS7 was found. Excluded candidates failed because framework anions moved or because the reaction against lithium metal gave metallic products. This is a computational prediction, not a proven material.

data.text: The agent proposed nine selenide-substituted derivatives of Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4 and screened them for stability, electronic insulation and lithium diffusion. Several candidates were rejected because the framework moved in molecular dynamics with chlorine or oxygen diffusing at up to about 40 percent of lithium, and others were rejected for being non-passivating against lithium metal with metallic decomposition products and reaction energies around 2.1 to 2.5 eV per atom. Three related candidates remained with near-zero energy above the hull and insulating band gaps: Li6P2SeS7 with energy above the hull about -0.01 eV per atom and band gap about 2.5 eV, Li12P4SeS15 with energy above the hull about 0.00 eV per atom and band gap about 2.6 eV, and Li7P3SeS10 with energy above the hull about 0.02 eV per atom and band gap about 2.4 eV. Molecular dynamics found lithium diffusion tied to the parent with diffusion ratios of about 0.66, 0.82 and 1.07 respectively. The agent concluded these selenide substitutions give computationally predicted stable insulating frameworks with lithium transport comparable to the parent but without a clear improvement.
